items.title: DSA kya hai aur interview mein kaise use hota hai
items.one_idea: DSA is two things, a data structure (how data is organised) and an algorithm (the steps that use it), and an interview checks whether your steps still work when the data is huge: 10 lakh sorted names take up to 1,000,000 checks one by one but about 20 with halving.
items.spoken_hook: Interviewer ने पूछा: 10 लाख names में एक name, 20 steps में कैसे ढूँढोगे?
items.hook_source: carried-over LearnAI hypothesis, first DSA test; hookscore 46.5 WEAK, no DEALBREAKER
items.visual_idea: A long row of name tiles with a magnifier moving one tile at a time and a step counter climbing toward 1,000,000, crossed out in red; then the same row halved again and again, the counter stopping at 20; chips DATA STRUCTURE (the row) and ALGORITHM (the halving moves) land on the objects when named.

items.title: Big-O: steps ka growth, seconds nahi
items.one_idea: Big-O says how the number of steps grows when the input grows: one-by-one search grows in step with the data (10 lakh to 20 lakh names is 10 lakh to 20 lakh steps), halving adds one step, checking every pair quadruples when data doubles.

items.title: Space complexity: memory dekar time bachana
items.one_idea: Space complexity says how much extra memory an algorithm needs as the input grows, and the time-space trade-off is paying memory to save steps: finding a duplicate among 10 lakh numbers takes about 5 hundred billion pair checks with no extra memory, but 10 lakh steps if you spend memory on a set.
items.spoken_hook: Code अटक रहा था, memory बढ़ाते ही चल गया।
items.hook_source: relatable_stake rotation: d001 interviewer_asked, d002 surprising_fact; stake first, first teaching line (the 10 lakh numbers setup) follows with nothing between
items.hook_10s: Code अटक रहा था, memory बढ़ाते ही चल गया। मान लो 10{दस} लाख numbers हैं और duplicate ढूँढना है। इसे ही space और time का trade-off कहते हैं, देखो कैसे। [frame 0: 10 lakh number tiles on the left, a memory bar on the right empty, a step counter stuck high]

hook_candidates.hook: Code अटक रहा था, memory बढ़ाते ही चल गया।
Memory मुफ़्त नहीं है, पर time से सस्ती है।
10{दस} लाख numbers में duplicate कितनी memory में ढूँढोगे?

items.visual_idea: A row of 10 lakh number tiles. Left lane: every tile paired with every other tile by lines, a step counter racing toward 5 hundred billion, memory bar flat and tiny. Right lane: tiles dropped one by one into a growing shelf (the set), memory bar rising to about 4x, step counter stopping at 10 lakh; two bars (steps and memory) swap sizes between the lanes.
items.everyday_anchor: A shopkeeper who keeps a price list on the wall (more space used) instead of recalculating every price at the counter each time (more time).
items.example: EXAMPLE (researcher ran it, Python 3.12.3, counts not seconds): 10 lakh ints, duplicate check by comparing pairs: n(n-1)/2 = 499999500000 steps (formula run for n=1000: 499500, matches; n=10 lakh not run); with a set: 1000000 steps, set length 1000000, memory O(n). List scan of absent target: 1000000 comparisons, O(1) extra memory. Memory bytes vary by machine, so say 'about 4x the list container' and 'tens of MB' (getsizeof list 8000056 B vs set 33554648 B, container only). Optional cut-first second example for the catch beat: fib(30) naive 2692537 calls vs dict memo 59 calls, dict size 31.
facts_to_verify: Space complexity = memory an algorithm needs as input grows (Wikipedia Space complexity, fetched).
Trade-off = more space for less time, or the reverse (Wikipedia Space-time tradeoff, fetched).

Hash table lookup: average constant time, worst case O(n) (Wikipedia Hash table, fetched). That a Python set is a hash table is NOT verified: wiki.python.org/moin/TimeComplexity returned 404 twice, so do not claim 'set lookup is O(1)' as a Python fact; say 'a hash-based set' as our reasoning or drop the claim until a primary Python page loads.
sys.getsizeof counts only the object itself, not what it refers to (docs.python.org, fetched): say 'container only'.
Run the duplicate-check snippets again and show the real printed counts (1000000 and 499999500000 formula, checked at n=1000 as 499500); do not put bytes or seconds on screen as exact numbers.
The set also costs O(n) steps to build once; say it.
